issues.failure_explanation: Subordination of the constructed {\eta_i} to the cover {\pi_M^{-1}(U_i)} (with U_i the radius-\delta geodesic balls) would require \eta_i(x)\neq 0 to imply d_M(\pi_M(x),z_i)\le\delta. It fails: \tilde\eta_i(x)>0 only requires the tangential-at-z_i component to satisfy ||P(z_i)^T(x-z_i)||_2 < h\delta with h = 6/(1-qp^{-1}) = 6(1+q)/(1-q) \ge 6, and ||x-z_i||_2 < p\tau_M(z_i); a point x = v (or v plus a very short normal offset) with d_M(v,z_i) = 3\delta satisfies both constraints yet has \pi_M(x) = v outside U_i. The paper's own quantitative localization radius 72\delta/(1-q)^2 (used to bound |f-\hat f|) confirms the supports extend beyond radius \delta. The false assertion is, however, immaterial: the argument only uses \sum_i \eta_i = 1 and the localization property (loc), both independently established.

failure_location.quote: $\{\eta_i\}_{i=1}^K$ forms a partition of unity subordinate to  the cover $\{\pi^{-1}_{\mathcal{M}}(U_i)\}_{i=1}^K$ of $\mathcal{M}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'subordinate to the cover {\pi^{-1}_{\mathcal{M}}(U_i)}' by subordination to the enlarged cover {\pi^{-1}_{\mathcal{M}}(B_{\mathcal{M}}(z_i, C(q)\delta))} with C(q) = 72/(1-q)^2 from the localization property; all subsequent estimates and both theorems are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The stated subordination of the constructed partition of unity to the cover {\pi_M^{-1}(U_i)} is false; no quantitative estimate of the paper depends on it, since the error analysis relies only on the partition property and on the localization bound (loc) with its enlarged radius.
issues.title: Constructed partition of unity is claimed subordinate to the radius-delta cover, contradicting the paper's own localization radius
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence weakening of a decorative support claim; the localization estimate actually invoked (radius 72\delta/(1-q)^2), the oracle error O(\delta^\alpha), and every downstream rate are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: The Gating Lemma as stated in this source provides only a keep-or-reset map: FFN(h_t) = h_t for t in {1,...,k} and h_t mapped to [0; I_t^1; I_t^2; 1] otherwise. The proofs of Lemmas lem_sumD, lem_add, lem_cmulti, lem_sq and lem_pp each end by invoking this lemma to 'subtract off the constant (DM or M) only from columns D+1 to 2D (resp. 2D+1 to 3D)' while leaving every other entry of the embedding matrix intact. That token-selective affine subtraction is a different operation from the stated keep-or-reset map, and no stated result supplies it; the final displayed equalities of those proofs (the exact implemented matrices) are therefore unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: Then we apply the Gating Lemma \ref{Gatinglemma} to have a $\mathcal{FFN}(3)$ to subtract off the constant $DM$ in the $D+1$-th column.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add one contained lemma, proved by the same technique as the Gating Lemma (interval indicators of the token index built from the interaction rows I_t): an FFN realizing h_t \mapsto h_t - c e_1 on any prescribed set of token indices and h_t elsewhere, with weight bound O(\ell\|H\|_\infty); then invoke it in each subtraction step. Every statement and rate of the paper then holds verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The detailed constructions of the basic arithmetic operations (Lemmas lemsumD through lemdiv), and the proofs that chain them (Propositions repetatildei and approxetai, Theorems thmApprox and thmGeneralization) are incomplete as written: the constant-subtraction step in each construction is attributed to a lemma whose stated guarantee is a different operation. All the claims remain plausible but are not established by the cited tool.
issues.title: Arithmetic-operation proofs invoke the Gating Lemma for a token-selective constant subtraction it does not provide
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local variant of a construction the paper already cites and uses, with no new ideas, and every lemma statement, rate, and guarantee survives unchanged; hence the least complete resolution is minor.
